body.heading: About this poster
paragraphs: Free SparkKindly Kids how things work printable poster: How Bacteria Multiply.

This poster covers binary fission, the bacteria way of multiplying: one bacterium copies its DNA, stretches as the copies move apart, then pinches and splits into two identical bacteria — which is how a few bacteria can become millions so quickly.

body.heading: How to use this sheet
paragraphs: Print it big if you can and read it together, pointing to each label as you name it. Then cover the words and see how much you can explain from the pictures alone — that explaining-back is where the learning sticks.

body.heading: Talk about it
paragraphs: Why can bacteria numbers grow so fast?
Are the two new bacteria the same as the first one?

takeaway: Bacteria multiply by binary fission — copying their DNA and splitting into two identical cells.
materials: A printer and one sheet of paper (letter or A4) — or just a screen to view it on
supervision: Read together the first time: an adult reads the labels aloud and answers the questions the poster raises.
safetyNotes: A reading poster — no tools, parts or experiments. If you try a related activity afterwards, a grown-up leads.
Print at 100% size (not "fit to page") so the poster keeps its true proportions.
screenFreeExtension: Explain it back: after reading, put the poster away and tell a grown-up how it works in your own words — then draw your own version.
